title: NVIDIA NemoClaw Flaw Lets Attackers Hijack AI Agents Through DNS Rebinding
content_md: A critical vulnerability in NVIDIA NemoClaw, tracked as CVE-2026-65105, could let attackers hijack AI agents after a victim visits a malicious website. The issue combines an insecure Ollama network configuration with DNS rebinding, allowing unauthenticated access to the local model server and persistent poisoning of the model template used by OpenClaw agents . NemoClaw runs the OpenClaw AI agent in NVIDIA OpenShell sandboxes and supports Ollama for local inference. This arrangement allows developers to process prompts and code on hardware instead of sending data to a cloud API. NVIDIA NemoClaw Flaw OpenShell sandboxes run inside Docker containers; however, this creates a connectivity challenge: containers cannot reach an Ollama service listening only on the host loopback interface. To address that limitation, NemoClaw starts Ollama with OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0:11434 . The configuration makes the service accessible to containers, but it also binds Ollama to every network interface. NemoClaw reportedly describes the service as running on localhost:11434 , despite the underlying listener being reachable from the local network. Ollama exposes an HTTP API on port 11434 without authentication. Its security controls instead rely on CORS enforcement and Host-header validation to limit requests originating from web pages.
